correctness.rationale: Complete two-case derivation: k+3+r−(x+y+z) is exactly zero or one; direct substitution lists all r+3 solutions. Boundary uniqueness follows coordinate inequalities. The projected integer kernel has index c, and the boundary-difference determinant is (r+1)c, giving exact index r+1. Uniqueness of rational barycentric coordinates gives minimal denominator (r+1)/gcd(j,r+1). Independent exhaustive arithmetic enumeration covers 741 parameter pairs, not an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The family supplies an explicit arbitrarily large *necessary* normalization denominator with one distinct integral point on every coordinate edge. Prior unrestricted rational interpolation and general coin-partition counting do not state this sharp lattice-saturation law. Binner 2021 already disproved a proposed boundary-combination conjecture by a different method; no novelty is claimed for refuting it. Residual unindexed equivalents cannot be ruled out.

value.rationale: This is an exact classification of the whole sparse solution fiber with a sharp natural invariant: the saturation index and minimal rational interpolation denominators. The unbounded obstruction persists even when all three edge sets contain exactly one distinct point and span the full real solution plane. It provides a meaningful precise limitation of bounded-coefficient boundary reduction, not merely a negative type check, and illustrates the distinction between integer and rational affine reconstructions.
